text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, six activities — A33, A35, A36, A37, A38 and A39 — each ran in every trace (200 of 200). In the later window, A33, A35 and A36 each appear in about 47 in 100 traces (93–94 of 200) and A37, A38 and A39 in about 56 in 100 (111–113 of 200), while A30, A31 and A34 still appear in every trace in both windows. [OCC029, OCC031, OCC032, OCC033, OCC034, OCC035, OCC026, OCC027, OCC030]
- The six also stopped appearing jointly. Before, every pair of them co-occurred in 100 in 100 traces; in the later window, A33/A35/A36 still appear together whenever one of them does (co-occurrence about 46–47 in 100, equal to their participation), the same holds for A37/A38/A39 (about 55–56 in 100), but cross-pairs such as A33 with A37 or A35 with A38 now co-occur in only about 2–3 in 100 traces, and no trace contains none of the six. The order inside each sub-group stays mixed (no fixed order), as before. [REL002, REL005, REL008, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL019, REL023, REL026, REL027, REL028]
- A30 and A31 still enclose whichever sub-group runs. A30's outgoing transitions, previously only to A33, A35 and A36 (about 34, 36 and 29 per 100), now split between the two sub-groups (about 45 per 100 to A33/A35/A36, about 53 per 100 to A37/A38/A39); A33, A35 and A36, which never led directly to A31 before, now do so in about 24–34 per 100 of their outgoing transitions. [DIR030, DIR033, DIR035, DIR036]
- Distances compressed accordingly: the gap from A30 to A37, A38 or A39 fell from 4–5 steps (about half each) to 1–3 steps (about 28–37 in 100 per step), and the gap from A33, A35 or A36 to A31 fell from 4–5 steps to 1–3 steps. [LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG013, LAG019]
- Relative positions shifted with the shorter block: A33/A35/A36 now sit slightly later in the trace (mean relative position about 0.68 to 0.73–0.74) and A37–A39 slightly earlier (about 0.76–0.77 to 0.74), each measured only over the traces containing the activity. [POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the six-activity block between A30 and A31 — A33, A35, A36, A37, A38 and A39 — which every case executed in full in the earlier window, is no longer executed in full in the later window: about 46–47 in 100 cases run the sub-group A33 with A35 and A36, about 55–57 in 100 run A37 with A38 and A39, both sub-groups appear together in only about 2–3 in 100 cases, and essentially no case skips the block entirely. A30 still precedes and A31 still follows whichever sub-group runs, now 1–3 steps away instead of 4–5. [OCC029, OCC031, OCC032, OCC033, OCC034, OCC035, REL016, REL020, REL023, REL026, DIR030, LAG004, LAG007]

The change is shown directly rather than inferred: participation of all six activities drops from 100 in 100 traces to about 47/56 in 100 (each estimate backed by about 200 before vs 93–113 after traces, reference strength about 0.995), the pairwise co-occurrence collapse is observed relationally, A30's successor profile and the new direct edges into A31 match the same split, and the lag and position items agree. These indicators are computed from the same traces, so they corroborate one structural difference rather than serving as independent confirmations. [OCC029, OCC035, REL002, REL016, DIR030, DIR033, LAG004, POS003]

Other differences: A43 and A44 are executed and repeated more often in the later window (A44: mean 0.79 → 0.94 occurrences per trace, participation 63 → 68 in 100, recurrence 14 → 20 in 100; A43: mean 1.56 → 1.71); routing shares into A30 shifted within the A21–A24 cluster (A23 → A30 from about 48 to 61 per 100 of A23's outgoing transitions; A24 → A22 from about 22 to 34 per 100 while A24 → A30 fell from about 55 to 44 per 100); and successor shares moved among A11, A13 and A14 (A11 → A14 from about 42 to 27 per 100, A11 → A13 from about 26 to 38 per 100). The outgoing profile of A48 changed completely, but it rests on only 5 vs 7 outgoing transitions and is too rare to interpret. [OCC039, OCC040, DIR023, DIR024, DIR029, DIR011, DIR013, DIR048]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the choice between the two sub-groups is made upstream of A30 or reflects two case variants mixed in different proportions; the indicators show only that, per case, exactly one sub-group now runs between A30 and A31, not what selects it. [DIR030, REL016, REL026]
